exposure: Cesarean delivery for medical reasons vs. non-medical reasons
Women who underwent cesarean delivery due to medical reasons
cohort: Women who gave birth between January 2000 and December 2012 in Taiwan
finding: Women who underwent primary cesarean delivery, particularly for medical reasons, had an approximately 30% higher risk of developing coronary heart disease compared to those who had vaginal deliveries.
mod_finding: Women who had undergone primary CD, especially those who had undergone CD due to medical reasons, were associated with an ∼30% higher risk of CHD than those who had undergone VD.
